summary: ACCEPT. Moves the armed-segment pager's internal ET guard from 420 (07:00 ET) to 360 (06:00 ET). THIS FIXES A DEFECT I CREATED. In #842 I asked for the CRON schedule to widen from 11-21 to 10-21 UTC to buy an hour of pre-open warning, codex agreed with my reasoning, and NEITHER OF US GREPPED THE CALLEE. The wrapper carried its own guard refusing anything before 07:00 ET, so the widened cron fired 06:00-07:00 ET and exited 0 silently every time. Effective coverage never changed. The schedule was configured and not enforced -- a dead guard dominated by an earlier return, findable only by reading the thing being invoked. I changed a schedule without reading the script it calls. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION, RUN NATIVELY ON LINUX in a throwaway clone (a Windows run is void for a shell script -- established on #842 where path-form mangling produced a false negative I nearly reported as contradicting the author). Baseline 3 collected cases in this file, all passed. Mutant reverting 360 back to 420: 2 failed, 1 passed, killed by test_wrapper_opens_exactly_at_0600_et[06-00-True] AND by test_wrapper_header_names_the_effective_schedule_and_window. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 184d8b2f07de3b7b...; clone removed. THE BOUNDARY CONTROL IS GENUINELY TWO-WAY: parametrized [(05,59,False),(06,00,True)], so one variable with both outcomes reachable. An existence check on 06:00 alone could not have distinguished the bound. ⭐ THE HEADER COMMENT IS ITSELF PINNED BY A TEST, and that is the most valuable part of this PR. The wrapper's header had gone stale twice over -- it still documented the 11-21 cron line and a 07:00-16:30 window after #842 changed the schedule. A stale contract comment is precisely what let the false _fetch_open_positions docstring survive into #843, and pinning the header means this specific rot cannot recur silently. Both offset ranges in the comment are now correct: EDT 06:00-16:30 ET is 10:00-20:30 UTC and EST is 11:00-21:30 UTC, both inside the installed 10-21 cron window. COUNT RECONCILED, not waved through: the report said 6 passed and I measured 3. Both are right -- this file has 2 test functions yielding 3 collected cases, and the other 3 are in test_armed_segments_schedule_install.py from #842. No discrepancy in substance. ✅ CLOSED BEFORE MERGE -- THE NOTIFICATION PATH IS NOW PROVEN END TO END. The production selftest ran at 15:36:02 ET and printed SELFTEST_RC=0, but that alone proves INVOCATION only: 'SELFTEST push sent' is written to cron.log unconditionally on the line immediately after the call, so it is true whether or not anything was delivered. THE OPERATOR CONFIRMED ON HIS OWN DEVICE that the armed-segments SELFTEST notification ARRIVED. That is the only authority that can close a delivery question and it is now closed. ⭐ Recorded because the correction was possible: this record still said UNPROVEN when I wrote it, and I amended it BEFORE the PR merged rather than leaving a durable inaccuracy in the ledger -- the #827 pin carries a unit error I found too late to fix, and that is the mistake this avoids. THE FULL CHAIN IS NOW VERIFIED: script correct (#841, by execution against the live sudoers), scheduled (#842 -- one managed cron entry, wrapper executable with mode 100755 IN THE GIT INDEX not a hand-chmod, box TZ confirmed Etc/UTC so 10-21 really is 06:00-17:00 ET), window correct (#844, mutation-pinned on a two-way boundary), and DELIVERY confirmed by the operator. The production selftest ran at 15:36:02 ET and printed SELFTEST_RC=0, but 'SELFTEST push sent' is written to cron.log unconditionally on the line immediately after the call, so it proves INVOCATION and says nothing about DELIVERY. Only the operator's own device can close that, and at the time of this pin he has not yet confirmed. An unproven notification path is the same false-clean shape as the pager that had no cron entry at all. ⛔ DEPLOY: ops/** is not sync-only eligible -- explicit copy required. No service restart. No re-run of the schedule installer is needed; the cron line is unchanged by this PR.
